messages.subject: Error in predict.ds
parts:
Hi list,

I am trying to predict the ESW but I get an error even if I use exactly the same data that I introduced to run the detection function model.

The R code is the following:

ds_model <- ddf(method="ds",
            dsmodel=~mcds(key="hr", formula= ~ YEAR + log_SIZE + VISIBILITY),
            data=data_df, meta.data=list(width=1150))

data_df$esw_mrds <- predictds_model, newdata = data_df, compute = FALSE, int.range = NULL, esw = TRUE)

Error in predict.ds(model_larfus, newdata = new_data, compute = FALSE,  : 
fields or factor levels in `newdata` do not match data used in fitted model


As you see, the data are exactly the same. Before trying to predict this ESW I have calculates another one and I did not get any error.

Do you know what might be going on?

Thank you in advance!

Isabel G-B

messages.author: f2122b34f1aa6e95
messages.subject: Re: [distance-sampling] Re: Error in predict.ds
parts:
Isabel

Without your dataset, I tried to reconstruct your problem using the "golftee" data included in the mrds package.  As you are using single observer data (method="ds"), I use the example code provided with the function ddf.ds(), adding a couple of lines to make sex and size factor covariates (as you have covariates in your detection function):

data(book.tee.data)
region <- book.tee.data$book.tee.region
egdata <- book.tee.data$book.tee.dataframe
samples <- book.tee.data$book.tee.samples
obs <- book.tee.data$book.tee.obs
egdata$size <- as.factor(egdata$size)
egdata$sex <- as.factor(egdata$sex)
result <- ddf(dsmodel = ~mcds(key = "hn", formula = ~sex+size),
              data = egdata[egdata$observer==1, ], method = "ds",
              meta.data = list(width = 4))
summary(result,se=TRUE)
plot(result,main="cds - observer 1")
my.pred <- predict(result, newdata=egdata[egdata$observer==1,], esw=TRUE)

> head(my.pred$fitted)
[1] 2.475936 2.475936 1.534598 2.475936 2.475936 3.876284

As you see, I cannot reproduce the problem you report.

Are you treating the covariates in your model as factors or continuous variables; perhaps check there.

Isabel

I'm none the wiser.  Now, I'm only guessing.  Here are two guesses I would investigate:

- were there any errors associated with the call to ddf(); that is, does the object ds_model2 look OK?

- you are truncating your fit at 1150 (m?).  I wonder if predict() does anything sensible with respect to predicting ESW for detections made >1150?

Perhaps more clever mrds folks on the list will have smarter ideas.
